I need to decide whether to bid on SHORT_LINE in this auction.

I have $546 and p2 has $225. The current bid is $70. I previously planned to bid up to $99 and mortgage the property if I won. The mortgage value of a railroad is $100.

A $71 bid nets $29 cash after mortgaging. If p2 wins at $70, they would have $155 left and could mortgage for $100 to reach $255. The goal is to force them to pay more and drain their cash while keeping the option to mortgage if I win under $100.

p2 owns dangerous properties: Park Place and Boardwalk with three houses each, plus the full orange monopoly. I own light blue with four, three, and three houses respectively. States Avenue is unmortgaged but not part of a pink monopoly since p2 holds St. Charles and Virginia. Ventnor is unmortgaged.

No yellow monopoly exists for me since p2 mortgaged Atlantic and Marvin Gardens. The green monopoly is split and mostly mortgaged. I am now deciding whether to bid $71 or drop out.

Oriental Avenue with four houses pays $400. Vermont Avenue with three houses pays $270. Connecticut Avenue with three houses pays $300. These are substantial rent amounts.

p2's orange monopoly with four houses each pays $750, $750, and $800. That totals $2300 in combined rent. Park Place with three houses pays $1100. Boardwalk with three houses pays $1400. Landing on these properties would drain my entire cash balance.

I can mortgage States Avenue for $70 and Ventnor for $130. Selling the ten houses on my light blue properties would net $250. That combined with my $546 cash gives me roughly $896 in liquid assets.

The total liquid assets are roughly $1156. Boardwalk with three houses pays $1400, which exceeds this amount, so landing there would still bankrupt me even fully liquidated.
